paper.title_en: Probing quadruple deformation in transitional nuclei via angular momentum projection
paper.abstract_en: Within the interacting boson model (IBM), a geometric analysis of transitional nuclei is carried out through angular momentum projection of the intrinsic coherent state. The results indicate that <math><mi>K</mi></math>-mixing effects in the calculations are typically negligible, validating the use of <math><mi>K</mi></math>-fixed projection for semiclassical analyses of the spin dependence of quadrupole deformation in the IBM. Further analysis indicates that in a rotating transitional system, quadrupole deformation is stretched with increasing angular momentum, providing a geometrically intuitive perspective on the commonly observed Jacobi-type transitions, as exemplified by the case studies of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Gd</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>160</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Dy</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>162</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The method is additionally applied to the yrast states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Os</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>170</mn></mmultiscripts></math> to probe quadrupole deformation changes linked to the observed low-spin <math><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> anomaly behavior, demonstrating the capability of IBM-based angular momentum projection in interpreting exotic collective phenomena.
